issue.title: Admit original Nanaware2024 lymph/DC quantities with sample and preparation distinctions
issue.body:
Presto needs independent quantitative native-peptide and APC presentation measurements to test processing and a separately fitted MS-response term. The original Nanaware2024 workbooks and processed identification files are now recovered, but are not yet available through a released canonical Hitlist source/recipe.

Primary study: [PMID38848214 / PMC11233987](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11233987/), DOI10.1016/j.celrep.2024.114311. Deposits: PXD051024, PXD044801, PXD044885, PXD051618/MSV000094586 and PXD052267/MSV000094761.

## Recovered evidence

- All seven original workbooks, primary XML/rights metadata, human community SDRF and nine original mzIdentML files are pinned by URL, size and SHA256. No RAW acquisition or author/private access was required. PMC metadata records CC BY-NC-ND.
- Human S6(a) native lymph has1,783peptide-feature rows and1,783positive area cells. Its side-by-side protein summary has a different row order and derives from those native peptides; it is not independent precursor abundance.
- Mouse DC S4(e) has separate database-search and spectral-library blocks:1,581/1,020feature rows and2,536/4,632positive area cells. Separate intensity columns are retained. These algorithms reuse acquisitions and must not become independent replicates.
- Original deposited search entries provide3,430protein-reference records and23,455peptide-evidence alternatives across human/DC files. These are candidate origins, not measured precursor identities.
- Independent original XML decoding verifies121,346source cells and all32,995emitted quantity cells, including missing values, plus every deposited reference/evidence entry. PRIDE inventories reconcile4/13/50files and MassIVE132/44files.

## Metadata that must survive admission

1. Human material is native extracellular lymph from IBD subjects, not the free intracellular APC pool. Sample1 donor/pooling identity and pairing with the five-patient proteomics summaries remain unresolved.
2. DCs were expanded using B16-FLT3-L treatment before isolation. Do not label them untreated baseline APCs. Preserve mouse species/strain, cervical versus mesenteric origin, DC enrichment, MHC-II/I-Ab capture and intervention scope. No per-sample machinery KO state is supplied; unknown is not wildtype.
3. DC table description declares3cervical/6mesenteric replicates plus controls, but the quantity headers export3+3channels. Preserve this unresolved correspondence; do not manufacture samples. A methods paragraph also uses control/DSS lymph wording that does not establish DSS assignment for these DC channels.
4. Primary human native-peptide methods specify Q-Exactive HF; the community SDRF specifies Fusion Lumos. Preserve the source conflict instead of silently selecting one instrument.
5. Mouse S4(n) no-enzyme searches reuse files described under enzymatically digested proteomics. Do not treat these as native biological cleavage labels until actual preparation is resolved. Search enzyme settings are distinct from laboratory digestion.
6. Preserve source scores/filter provenance, modified forms, charges, alternative parents, raw coordinates, observed/missing/zero states, areas versus intensities and unqualified normalization. Predicted class-II cores are not measured registers. Same anatomy does not establish an exact specimen/aliquot join.

## Acceptance and downstream use

- Add a source family through the shared EvidenceStore/catalog/bindings with immutable original assets, typed contexts/samples/assertions, independent source-block rows, observation/quantity cells and reference/identification alternatives. No private Presto workbook curator.
- Keep unreviewed workbook blocks as source-only assets. Source admission must not silently become training eligibility, inferred detection negatives or calibrated concentrations.
- Verify real-source cells independently and test side-by-side row mismatches, search-output dependence, missingness, unsupported forms, header drift and tampering.
- Follow with a registered endpoint-specific recipe for observable relative composition, explicit confidence/form aggregation, all-parent alternatives/dependence and prospective splits. Any biological comparison should share its objective and frozen MS observer between exact and sampled methods and retain simple sequence/condition controls.

This supports, but does not complete, the APC availability goal. Current biological scores are unchanged. Search by PXD051024, PMID38848214 and PMC11233987 found no existing source owner; broader sample-anchor issue #362 and MS-response issue #762 remain related.

issue.title: Normalize materials, interventions, lineage and assay protocols
issue.body:
Parent: #733. **PR 3 of 6**, depends on PR 2. Give experimental context typed identities and source assertions.

### Scope
- Introduce study/arm/material, donor/specimen/acquisition lineage, material-to-assay and protocol/run relations. Preserve unresolved, pooled and ambiguous links without filling identifiers from PMID or cell-line name.
- Migrate curated knockout/knockdown/overexpression, cytokine/drug/infection/stimulation, control, cell type and sample MHC assertions into typed concurrent factors; retain original scalar claims and citations.
- Put capture/digestion, enzyme, IP antibody, instrument, fragmentation, acquisition mode, search/FDR and binding/T-cell readout metadata on protocol/run at supported scope. Record whether values were reported per-run or study-wide.
- Distinguish tested MHC, presenting sample candidate set, independent cellular genotype and peptide restriction.

### Acceptance
- Every current condition/protocol field maps losslessly to a v2 relation or explicit unmapped report. Unknown is never untreated; concurrent factors remain concurrent.
- Source-linked lineage and MHC-role tests, including ambiguous arms and multi-allele samples. No invented donor/specimen/allele labels.
- Run format/lint/full tests; version bump, review, merge and PyPI deployment.


### Availability datasets: homogeneous study/sample metadata acceptance

User requirement from the Presto availability work: all important facts that
distinguish these studies/samples must survive in this shared curation system,
not only in paper-specific code or experiment notes. The [consumer contract](https://github.com/pirl-unc/presto/blob/932ccefceda4aa82e98a43fbe01ebb8896e9dfec/docs/study_curation_contract.md)
and its PXD057588 acceptance case extend this existing PR3 scope; do not create a
parallel Presto registry.

Required structured coverage, with source text, normalized value, evidence locator
and supported scope:

- Biological material and system: species by role, strain, cell type/ontology,
  cell line/clone, primary/transformed state, tissue/compartment, disease/state,
  relevant reported donor/animal characteristics, isolation history; monoculture,
  coculture or mixed material, all participating populations, measured population,
  partner roles, separation/contact and purity/contamination evidence.
- Concurrent conditions: component-loss state and its validation, cytokine/drug/
  stimulus, dose/unit/duration/order, explicit control type and supported matched
  control relation. Reuse existing condition vocabulary. Unknown is not a
  reference genotype, untreated state or explicit absence.
- Measured pool: MHC-bound, proteasome-associated, native intracellular or secreted
  peptides, bulk digest peptides/proteins or purified assay. Keep capture pool,
  compartment, enrichment, IP target/antibody, native recovery versus digestion
  and sample-input amount at assay scope.
- Sample-to-file relationships: donor/specimen/preparation/aliquot/arm, assay,
  multiplex channel, fraction, run, biological versus technical replicate and
  batch. Preserve many-to-many links, pooling, ambiguity and reuse/reanalysis.
  Use pinned SDRF metadata where available; it does not replace biochemical scope.
- MHC roles remain separate: tested molecule, genotype, presenting candidate set,
  introduced molecule, capture specificity and peptide restriction/evidence.
- Search and quantification processing: software/version, reference hash/species,
  modifications/search space, FDR/threshold **and its level**, contaminants/decoys,
  direct MS/MS versus matching/imputation, raw versus normalized quantity, units,
  encoding, normalization/reference/batch, calibration applicability and denominator.
- Selection/missingness: not searched, searched/unobserved, actual stated censor
  bound, failed QC, missing channel, filtered row, imputed and measured zero.
  Preserve complete-case and contamination filters rather than erasing their effect.

Assertions distinguish reported facts, curated normalization, inference/default,
unknown, explicit absence, not applicable, ambiguity and conflicting evidence.
A study-wide value cannot be broadcast to all arms without evidence. Annotation
confidence and source-to-sample attribution confidence remain different axes.
Source/row IDs and observation-process facts are not automatically model features.

**Concrete regression case: PXD057588**
([primary study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12616400/)):

- Query measured macrophages separately from measured tumor cells after coculture;
  retain the partner and naive/monoculture comparison. A coculture label must not
  invent the source cell of a peptide or a resolved population identity.
- Keep MHC-I immunopeptidomics and global proteomics as separate measurements with
  explicit material links. Do not label the former total intracellular peptides.
- Preserve quantitative channels, baseline grouping, source-reported q≤0.05,
  missing-channel exclusion and cell-attribution/contamination filtering.
- Selected calibrated targets have explicit applicability; broad relative
  measurements do not inherit copies-per-cell units.
- Actual deposited table/run/channel IDs and sample pairing must be curated before
  the source is training-eligible. The paper is evidence for admission work, not
  proof of a ready cohort.

Round-trip this metadata into frozen exports and downstream prediction provenance;
verify no source assertions disappear. Emit machine-readable coverage and per-task
missing-field/unsupported-join reasons. Include contrasting fixtures for Wolf-Levy
proteasome-associated MAPP, PXD017407 calibration, PXD013455 bulk digest scope, and
PXD056426/HAP1 control/loss arms. This augments the existing acceptance criteria;
implementation and new-source curation remain pending.


## Source-backed acceptance fixture: PXD057588 audited tables (2026-10-22)

The [completed initial source audit](https://github.com/pirl-unc/presto/blob/51b895eb3925de87df7710c7bd6c78d131c25697/experiments/2026-10-22_1410_codex_availability-source-audit/README.md) pins 17 original assets and independently verifies six quantitative workbooks plus community SDRF. This is evidence for implementing the shared catalog, not a claim that normalized source curation or training admission has shipped. Preserve the existing issue scope.

Required regression fixtures from actual source bytes:

- Scope channel identity to assay/plex: Tables 9 and 11 reuse the same nine TMT labels but eight map to different sample names. B4:B5 maps 128N to G3+ in Table 9 and C2+ in Table 11. Channel-only joins must fail; sample-name matches alone must not imply exact specimen/aliquot links.
- Scope genetic state to the affected population: Table 10 A2:A3 describes macrophage immunopeptidomics with MHC-I-loss GL261/CT2A tumor partners. The primary paper identifies H2-Kb/H2-Db loss in the tumor cells. Do not label measured macrophages as processing-gene knockouts; preserve differences in separation/attribution protocols.
- Preserve conflicts with cell locators: Table 8 A2 calls M2 pro-inflammatory despite the anti-inflammatory title; Table 10 A3 says n=3 but B5:L5 contains G1–G4, C1–C4, U1–U3. Do not silently correct, drop fourth channels or infer independent donors from label suffixes.
- Preserve incomplete SDRF scope: 72 rows × 45 columns cover only six of 50 raw files, all E38 CD45-negative tumor runs. Treatment is not available. Labels 1–12 are not independently established donor identities. Table 12 includes untreated controls even though SDRF source names all include cocult. Retain uncertainty instead of broadcasting treatment.
- Repeated SDRF headers are positional fields (three template, four modification fields). Workbook horizontal panels have independent sequence keys; Table 8 has 157 selected-panel rows all differing from the same-row primary sequence. Never join them solely by worksheet row.
- Keep complete-case filtering, relative intensity/log2 representations, search-confidence scope, parent ambiguity and calibration applicability. These six tables do not measure free intracellular concentration.

Use the pinned raw sources, inventories with cell coordinates and verification bundle linked in the report as acceptance inputs. Round-trip the distinctions through shared normalized records and frozen exports; until that works, source admission remains pending.


### Quantitative protocol scope follow-up — 2026-10-22

The [PXD057588 reconciliation](https://github.com/pirl-unc/presto/blob/30cc5368bfa58b936339c3e5600309625831d851/experiments/2026-10-22_1601_codex_pxd057588-quantity-reconciliation/README.md) now independently verifies every one of
200,724 primary fold-change calculations. Preserve the protocol distinction in the
shared system: global digest-peptide quantities use channel-total normalization;
MHC-elution quantities in these tables do not. Control group membership is
contrast-specific (including separate tumor-line controls in Table 12). Derived
quantity lineage/normalization coverage is detailed in #737 and the [shared contract](https://github.com/pirl-unc/presto/blob/30cc5368bfa58b936339c3e5600309625831d851/docs/study_curation_contract.md).

The source-specific material acceptance cases still apply: measured macrophage
versus tumor partner, partner-specific MHC-I loss, assay/plex-scoped channel IDs,
independent panels and unresolved specimen links. This thread is supplying audited
source evidence to the canonical PR3/PR4 work, not publishing a parallel schema.

issue.title: engineering_drift_audit: 71 arms silent on an engineering column a sibling asserts
issue.body:
Split out of #586 / #587, where `hitlist.qc.engineering_drift_audit` was added and immediately surfaced this.

> **Kept current.** This body is rewritten whenever the audit changes, rather than corrected in a comment — a stale instruction in an issue body is the same trap #587 hit four times: guidance that no longer matches the data or no longer loads. Last verified against Hitlist 1.82.11 / #720: **55 findings across 9 studies**, 39 `error` / 16 `warn`.

## The rule

An arm that is **silent** (`""`) on an `ENGINEERING_CONDITION_COLUMNS` value a **same-material sibling asserts** is flagged. Since #576 the engineered flag is per arm, so one blanked arm is already the #586 defect: `""` means "not established", the arm stops satisfying `is_engineered_material()`, and `resolve_sample_expression_anchor` hands it the reference line's RNA at **tier 1** — reported as RNA measured in the sample — while its sibling correctly resolves at tier 2.

`none` is a curated claim of absence and passes. PMID 40113210's `hap1_wildtype` is the worked example: it sits beside eleven knockout siblings and does **not** flag, because someone curated `none` onto it.

Run it with `hitlist qc engineering-drift [--severity warn|error]`, or find it under `engineering_drift` in `hitlist qc`.

## What it flags today

| PMID | findings | err | warn | columns | study |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 31495665 | 20 | 6 | 14 | mhc_context, transfection | Abelin 2019 — MAPTAC HLA-II + class I |
| 32350084 | 19 | 19 | 0 | mhc_context | van Balen 2020 — HLA-DP allelic variants |
| 34428180 | 5 | 3 | 2 | knockout_genes, mhc_context, transduction | Son 2021 — mouse transplant tolerance |
| 38480730 | 5 | 5 | 0 | transfection | Gomez-Zepeda 2024 — Thunder-DDA-PASEF |
| 36010968 | 2 | 2 | 0 | genetic_variants, transfection | Vadakekolathu 2022 — SaOS-2 p53 |
| 29769354 | 1 | 1 | 0 | overexpression_genes | Sanz-Bravo 2018b — ERAP2 overexpression |
| 30778243 | 1 | 1 | 0 | mhc_context | Koutsakos 2019 — influenza A/B/C |
| 34006841 | 1 | 1 | 0 | mhc_context | Hensen / Habel 2021 — HLA-A*24:02 |
| 36796642 | 1 | 1 | 0 | mhc_context | Pyke / SHERPA 2023 |

The exact set is in `tests/data/engineering_drift_baseline.yaml`, keyed `<condition_id>|<column>|<severity>` and asserted by **equality** in `tests/test_qc.py` — new drift fails CI, an entry fixed in the YAML but left in the baseline fails too, and a `warn` that becomes an `error` cannot reuse its entry.

**Changelog of removals** — each recorded so the falling count is auditable rather than mysterious:

- *71 → 69:* **PMID 27862975** dropped out. Its siblings asserted only `soluble_mhc`, a capture token, so nothing was engineered on either side and no tier differed — those findings were never drift.
- *69 → 66:* **PMID 33592498**'s three parental class-I arms (`hrog02_parental_class_i`, `hrog17_parental_class_i`, `ra_parental_class_i`) dropped out because #584 curated `condition_transduction: "none"` onto them. **This is the first real fix of debt recorded here**, and it is shape A resolved exactly as intended: a genuine parental arm beside a transduced sibling, annotated with the claim of absence rather than left silent. The baseline-equality assertion caught the stale entries on merge and named all three.
- *66 → 59:* **#716** recorded seven source-backed `none` claims for control arms in PMIDs 27371725, 30573663, 31092671, 32161166 and 36215666. The audit fell from 47 `error` / 19 `warn` to 43 / 16, with no change to any arm's engineered-material verdict or expression tier. PMID 29769354 remains open under #715 because its PF-GFP control is transduced.
- *59 → 55:* **#720** recorded four source-backed `none` claims for the parental wild-type THP-1 and primary hMDM arms in PMID 39438697. The audit fell from 43 `error` / 16 `warn` to 39 / 16. The four arms retained their unengineered verdicts and expression-anchor tiers.

## The remedies, and what the loader demands of each

Every remedy below was verified by running it through `load_pmid_overrides()`; `tests/test_qc.py` keeps them honest.

| remedy | the loader demands |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | only in the six engineering columns that permit it — **never** `condition_mhc_context` |
| `mhc_genotype` + `mhc_genotype_cell` + `mhc_genotype_source` | **all three together**; `mhc_genotype_cell` alone is rejected. `mhc_genotype` is ploidy-audited and checked against `mhc_genotype_complete_loci` |
| `sample_group` | on **every** arm of the study, and **not** one group per arm — so it **cannot** separate a two-arm study at all |

That last constraint decides the approach for 30778243, 34006841 and 36796642 (2–3 arms each): `sample_group` is unavailable to them, so the `mhc_genotype` trio is the only route.

## Two shapes of work

**A. A genuine wild-type or untreated arm beside an engineered sibling** — remedy `none`. Still a positive claim about an experiment, so it needs its own Methods check; no bulk application. The THP-1 wild-type and primary hMDM arms of 39438697 were cleared in #720; PMID 36215666's mock and siCTRL controls were cleared in #716.

**B. Arms that are different materials grouped together.** `sample_group` is unset on **all 9 remaining** studies, so a study's arms collapse into one group unless `mhc_genotype` or a context column separates them. 38480730 is the clearest: HeLa, a commercial human plasma pool, JY, Raji and SK-MEL-37 in one group, where the single transfected arm makes the other five look silent.

31495665 (MAPTAC) and 32350084 (HLA-DP variants) are together **39 of the 55** and are probably mostly shape B — each arm is a different mono-allelic construct.

## Why expression tiers are NOT demoted on silence

**The baseline is not "accepted forever"** — it is debt with a known reason it cannot be paid by code alone.

The obvious fix, demoting an arm to tier 2 whenever a same-material sibling is engineered, would key expression resolution off **this audit's grouping**, which shape B shows is unreliable. Demoting 38480730's five arms would report *the wrong parent line's RNA as a surrogate* for four unrelated materials — a new and less visible error than the one it fixes.

So: **fix the grouping first, then reconsider resolution.** Until material identity is trustworthy, the honest behaviour is what ships today — those arms resolve at tier 1 and the audit says loudly which are suspect.

## Known gaps the audit deliberately does not catch

- **`condition_mhc_context` cannot state absence.** It is the one engineering column `NONE_PERMITTED_CONDITION_COLUMNS` excludes, so an arm whose MHC genuinely is not introduced has no token to say so and its finding cannot be cleared by curation at all. Fixing that means permitting `none` there — a vocabulary change worth its own discussion.
- **A capture-only `condition_mhc_context` is not treated as silence**, for the same reason. PMID 28514659's `721_221_transfectant_shla_b_46_01` and `..._b_15_01` are 721.221 **transfectants** curated `soluble_mhc` alone, so they read as unengineered and are not flagged.

## Suggested order

1. Resolve PMID 29769354's PF/PF-GFP arm identity in #715 before any absence claim.
2. 28514659's two transfectant arms, above.
3. Shape B via the `mhc_genotype` trio for the 2–3 arm studies (30778243, 34006841, 36796642).
   *(33592498 is done — #584 resolved its three via `none`.)*
4. 38480730 — the clearest multi-material group, and the best test of whether fixing grouping is enough to revisit tier resolution.
5. 31495665 and 32350084 last: 39 of the 55, and worth deciding the MAPTAC / DP-construct convention once rather than per arm.

Every fix removes its entry from `tests/data/engineering_drift_baseline.yaml` in the same PR, which the equality assertion enforces.

issues.title: Flat experimental-condition columns on samples, observations and training rows
issues.body:
## Problem

The only machine-readable condition fields on an exported row are
`perturbation` (the curated string with an `unperturbed` prefix stripped) and
`condition_category` (one coarse bucket per arm). Selecting "every ERAP2
knockout arm", "every vehicle control" or "every arm on both IFN-γ and TNF"
means parsing prose. Three concrete losses, all present in the corpus today:

1. **A coarse bucket cannot separate two arms inside it.** `IFN-gamma 100
   IU/mL 24h` and `IFN-gamma 100 ng/ml 72h` are one `IFN_gamma_treatment`
   value. `export._select_best_candidate` accepts a scoring tie when the tied
   candidates' `condition_category` values agree, so one of two genuinely
   different arms is first-picked silently.
2. **One bucket per arm cannot hold two simultaneous factors.** `TAP1 knockout
   + Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv infection` categorizes as
   `TAP_perturbation`; the infection reaches no exported column.
3. **`simplify_condition` blanks everything after `unperturbed — `.** Right for
   a culture-medium annotation, wrong for the HLA-DM co-transfection that 42
   arms carry and 4 arms explicitly lack. All 46 report
   `condition_category == "unperturbed"`.

## Proposal

Add a flat block of condition columns, authored directly on `ms_samples`
records and exported under the same names, declared once in a
`hitlist/conditions.py` registry that feeds validation, the empty-frame
schemas, the observation join, and the training-table defaults.

Identity and interpretation: `condition_id`, `condition_status`,
`condition_evidence`, `condition_reference`, `condition_control`,
`condition_control_for`, `condition_combination`.

Independent factors: knockout / knockdown / overexpression genes, genetic
variants, transfection, transduction, cytokines, drugs, infection,
stimulation, antigen exposure, background, MHC context, culture, material,
labeling.

Rules that make the block trustworthy rather than merely present:

- `""` means *not established*; it never means untreated. `none` is a positive
  claim of absence, permitted only where a field supports one. `unspecified`
  means the intervention happened and its target is unnamed.
- Multi-valued cells are sorted, unique, `;`-separated, and mean *all of these
  apply* — never a union of alternatives.
- `condition_evidence` separates normalizing existing curated wording
  (`curated_text`) from reading the paper (`primary_source`, which requires a
  locator). Sample-annotation coverage and peptide-attribution coverage are
  reported separately; neither is evidence for the other.

Additive: `condition`, `condition_category`, `perturbation`, `is_control_arm`,
`arm_resolution` and the `apm_*` columns keep their documented legacy
meanings. The prose classifiers stay until a structured derivation has been
compared against the whole curated population.

Spec: `tasks/condition-model-spec.md`.

issues.title: condition_category and the apm_* block are derived from different normalizations of condition, so they disagree on 51 samples
issues.body:
## Problem

`generate_ms_samples_table()` derives two things from a sample's curated `condition` string, but from **different normalizations**, so they disagree:

- `perturbation` / `condition_category` — computed from the simplified condition, blanked whenever `condition.startswith("unperturbed")`.
- the `apm_*` block — computed from the **raw** `condition`.

So a sample can simultaneously report `condition_category == "unperturbed"` and `apm_erap2_perturbed == True`. After the #353 fix, **51 of 688 samples** are still in that state.

## Two distinct sub-cases

The corpus uses a consistent curator convention for `unperturbed`-prefixed conditions:

| form | count | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unperturbed — X` | 314 | X *annotates the baseline* — `— RPMI-1640`, `— direct ex vivo`, `— snap-frozen surgical resection`, `— baseline` |
| `unperturbed + X` | 7 | X is a **treatment that was applied** |
| bare `unperturbed` | 241 | — |

**a) The `+` form is silently discarded.** All 7 are `unperturbed + IFN-gamma (2000 U/mL, 3d)` (MEL2/MEL3/MEL15/GBM7/GBM9/GBM11/ccRCC Pat9). IFN-γ *was* applied, yet `perturbation` is blanked and `condition_category` reads `unperturbed`. These samples are labelled as controls when they are the treated arm.

**b) The `—` annotation leaks into the APM flags.** 44 dash-form samples get an APM flag from text that describes the baseline, not a treatment:

```
42x  unperturbed — HLA-DM co-transfected          -> apm_hla_dm_perturbed=True
 1x  unperturbed — Hap10 (low-activity) ERAP1 background -> apm_erap1_perturbed=True
 1x  unperturbed — natural ERAP2 genotype         -> apm_erap2_perturbed=True
```

`natural ERAP2 genotype` is a germline genotype, not a perturbation. This is the same "control arm flagged as a knockout" failure #353 is about, reached by a different route.

## Proposed fix

Give the APM classifier the **same** normalized string `condition_category` uses, and teach that normalization the `+` form:

- `unperturbed + X` → perturbation is `X` (treatment applied)
- `unperturbed — X` / `unperturbed (X)` / bare → perturbation is `""` (baseline)

Then `perturbation`, `condition_category`, and the `apm_*` block agree by construction — one source of truth instead of two.

The raw `condition` column is unchanged, so the annotation text stays available for audit.

## Acceptance criteria

- No sample reports `apm_perturbed=True` while `condition_category == "unperturbed"`.
- The 7 IFN-γ samples report `condition_category == "IFN_perturbation"` and are not labelled controls.
- `unperturbed — natural ERAP2 genotype` reports `apm_perturbed=False`.
- The `condition` column is untouched.

issues.title: APM per-gene flags are contaminated by study-level perturbations: control arms flagged as knockouts
issues.body:
## Problem

`apm_columns_for_sample()` derives the per-gene APM flags from the sample's own `condition` **unioned with the parent study's `perturbations` list**:

```python
# hitlist/export.py:432
row.update(
    apm_columns_for_sample(
        condition,
        perturbations=study_perturbations,   # <-- study-level, not sample-level
    )
)
```

For any study that curates a *panel* of perturbations, the study-level list names every gene in the panel, so **every arm of that study — including the untreated control — is flagged as perturbed for every gene.**

## Reproduction

Shapiro 2025 HAP1 APM CRISPR KO panel (PMID 40113210), 12 arms:

```python
from hitlist.export import generate_ms_samples_table
s = generate_ms_samples_table()
sub = s[s['pmid'].astype(str) == '40113210']
print(sub[['sample_label','condition_category','apm_perturbed',
           'apm_erap1_perturbed','apm_genes_perturbed']].to_string(index=False))
```

```
 sample_label  condition_category          apm_perturbed  apm_erap1_perturbed  apm_genes_perturbed
HAP1 wildtype  unperturbed                          True                 True  b2m;tap1;tap2;tapbp;erap1;pdia3;calr;canx;irf2;ganab;sppl3
  HAP1 B2M KO  MHC-I_loss_B2M                       True                 True  b2m;tap1;tap2;tapbp;erap1;pdia3;calr;canx;irf2;ganab;sppl3
 HAP1 TAP1 KO  TAP_perturbation                     True                 True  b2m;tap1;tap2;tapbp;erap1;pdia3;calr;canx;irf2;ganab;sppl3
HAP1 ERAP1 KO  ERAP1_perturbation                   True                 True  b2m;tap1;tap2;tapbp;erap1;pdia3;calr;canx;irf2;ganab;sppl3
... all 12 arms identical ...
```

The wildtype control claims `apm_erap1_perturbed=True`. Every arm claims all 11 genes.

## Blast radius (current corpus, v1.45.0)

- **184 of 688 `ms_samples` rows, spanning 22 PMIDs**, are flagged `apm_perturbed=True` while their own `condition_category` is `unperturbed`.
- 12 samples claim all 11 genes at once; 17 claim 2.

Affected control arms include `721.221-B*51:01 wildtype` (flagged `erap1;erap2`), `C1R HLA-B*40:02 (WT)` (flagged `erap2`), `A375 melanoma (untreated)` (flagged `erap1`), `A549 lung cancer (untreated)` (flagged `ifn_gamma;tnf_alpha`), `mouse splenocytes (WT)` (flagged `hla_do`), and all 11 `MAPTAC-HLA-*` samples (flagged `hla_dm`).

issues.title: Class-II 'implausible' threshold at ≥31aa flags ~13K legitimate Stražar 2023 peptides
issues.body:
## Background

v1.30.17 (#201) introduced four severity tiers for `mhc_class_label_severity`. The class-II `implausible` cutoff is currently:

> class II ≤4 or **≥31** aa → implausible

After the v1.30.20 PTM-suffix fix, the production parquet has **16,885 class-II rows tagged implausible**. The breakdown:

| PMID | Source | Rows | Study |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 37301199 | supplement | **13,268** | Stražar 2023 — HLA-II mono-allelic |
| 31495665 | supplement | 1,600 | Abelin 2019 — MAPTAC (class II portion) |
| 33968037 | iedb | 858 | TNBC IFNγ class II |
| 33043033 | iedb | 414 | IFN-induced class II changes on DR molecules |
| (other) | iedb | ~745 | various |

**78% are Stražar 2023 alone**, all from the curated paper supplement (`hitlist/data/supplementary/strazar_2023_hla2.csv`). Length distribution there:

```
count    308,418
mean      19.3 aa
max       51 aa
13,268 rows >= 31 aa
```

These aren't curation drift — the Stražar paper specifically reports mono-allelic class-II ligands up to 51aa.

## Why this matters

Users who pass `--exclude-class-label-implausible` (or `load_observations(exclude_class_label_implausible=True)`, both shipped in v1.30.18) currently lose ~13K legitimate Stražar mono-allelic class-II peptides. That's exactly the high-quality training data the filter is meant to preserve.

## Options

**A. Raise the implausible threshold** to `≥35` or `≥40`:
- Most class-II ligand papers report up to 30aa; HLA-DM-edited / unconventional class-II peptides extend to ~40-50aa per the literature.
- A threshold of `≥40` would keep ~16,400 of the 16,885 currently-implausible rows in `ok`/`borderline`, dropping only ~485 rows that are >=40aa — which are still rare enough to be worth flagging.
- Symmetric concern: raising the threshold lets through actually-mislabeled rows (class-I peptides with class-II label that happen to be 31-39aa) — but those would already be implausible-as-class-I rows (≥18aa class I), so they're caught regardless.

**B. Add a `borderline-long` tier** to mark 31-50aa as worth flagging but not implausible. Doubles the column complexity for marginal benefit.

**C. Per-source-organism / per-PMID override.** Heavy machinery; skip.

**D. Status quo** — accept that the implausible filter drops ~13K Stražar rows and document it.

## Recommendation

**Option A with threshold `≥40`** is the cleanest. The literature is reasonably consistent on \"normal\" class-II being ≤30aa, but reports of DM-edited / extended class-II ligands routinely span into the 30-40aa range. `≥40` lines up with the empirical break in Stražar's distribution (rows 30-39aa are fairly dense; 40+ aa are rare).

Symmetrically, the class-I implausible threshold of `≥18` should stay — bulged class-I peptides are well-documented but cap around 17aa.

Want me to ship A as v1.30.22? It's a one-line change in `hitlist/observations.py` plus adjusting the regression test.

## Related

- #201 (introduced the four-tier severity)
- #206 / v1.30.20 (the PTM-suffix fix that surfaced this signal cleanly)

While profiling #636, a bounded unit read audit intercepted test_scan_supplementary_parquet_roundtrip loading the real strazar_2023_hla2.csv. issues.title: Profile and optimize slowest parts of hitlist data build
issues.body:
## Motivation

The full `hitlist data build` (and the test suite that exercises the supplementary + observations path under coverage) is expensive. On this machine `./test.sh` takes ~8 minutes and `hitlist data build --force` is in the same order of magnitude. As we keep adding supplementary studies (PMID 37301199 / Stražar adds 308,418 rows alone) this cost will keep growing and will start to block iteration on curation changes.

## Goal

1. Profile a full `hitlist data build --force` end-to-end and identify the top 3-5 time-dominant stages (e.g. IEDB parse, CEDAR parse, supplementary scan + classification, observations join, peptide_mappings, mhcgnomes parsing, YAML override matching, parquet I/O).
2. For each hot stage, quantify: CPU time, wall time, peak memory.
3. Propose and land the highest-leverage optimization(s). Candidates to evaluate:
   - Vectorize remaining `.apply`/`iterrows` hot paths
   - Cache more aggressively (the mhcgnomes parse is already LRU-cached; check `classify_ms_row` and `classify_allele_resolution` hit rates)
   - Parallelize per-source classification (per-PMID or per-file)
   - Skip re-classifying rows when fingerprint of their inputs hasn't changed
   - Move supplementary CSV parsing to pyarrow/parquet on disk
4. Re-measure; target: at least 2x speedup on a full `--force` build on a warm dataset cache.

## Verification

- Before/after timings for `hitlist data build --force` (total + per-stage breakdown)
- Before/after timings for `./test.sh`
- No regressions in observation / sample counts or curation flags

issues.title: PyPI deploy blocked: project size quota exceeded (v1.34.0 unpublished)
issues.body:
## Problem

`./deploy.sh` (and direct `twine upload`) for **v1.34.0** fails at the PyPI upload step:

```
400 Bad Request
  400 Project size too large. Limit for project 'hitlist' total ...
```

v1.34.0 is **merged to main (#302) but NOT published to PyPI** (latest on PyPI is 1.33.2). This blocks every future release until resolved — it's a hard PyPI-side quota, not a transient error (the wheel uploads to 100% then PyPI rejects it).

## Root cause

Each release is ~90 MB (45.9 MB wheel + 45.9 MB sdist). The cumulative size across all published versions has hit PyPI's per-project total-size limit (10 GB default). The package is large because it **bundles big data files in the wheel**:

| File | Size |
|---|---|
| `hitlist/data/bulk_proteomics/bekker_jensen_2017_peptides.csv.gz` | 35.1 MB |
| `hitlist/data/supplementary/strazar_2023_hla2.csv` | 13.9 MB (**uncompressed**) |
| `hitlist/data/bulk_proteomics/bekker_jensen_2017_protein_abundance.csv.gz` | 4.4 MB |
| `hitlist/data/bulk_proteomics/ccle_nusinow_2020.csv.gz` | 1.7 MB |
| `hitlist/data/supplementary/abelin_2019_maptac_class2.csv` | 1.6 MB (uncompressed) |
| several `gomez_zepeda_2024_*.csv`, `shapiro_2025_*.csv` | uncompressed |

## Remedies

**Immediate (unblocks publishing — requires PyPI account action, cannot be done from code):**
1. **Request a project size-limit increase** for `hitlist` at https://github.com/pypi/support/issues (PyPI grants these routinely with a one-line justification), **or**
2. Delete old pre-1.30 releases on PyPI to reclaim space (destructive — breaks anyone pinned to them).

**Structural (shrinks every future release; reduces quota pressure):**
3. **Stop bundling the large bulk-proteomics / supplementary CSVs in the wheel.** They could be downloaded on first use into `~/.hitlist/` like the main corpus already is, instead of vendored into every release. Cutting the 35 MB + 14 MB files alone roughly halves the wheel.
4. **gzip the uncompressed CSVs** (`strazar_2023_hla2.csv` 14→~3 MB, `abelin_2019_maptac_class2.csv`, `gomez_zepeda_2024_*.csv`, `shapiro_2025_*.csv`) — a quick win even if they stay bundled.

## Status
- Code for v1.34.0 (`pmhc --species` / `--source-context`) is on `main`; only the PyPI publish is blocked.
- Recommend #1 (size-limit increase) to unblock now, then #3/#4 as a follow-up to stop the bloat recurring.

issues.title: Mono-allelic rows without specific allele should be resolved from paper supplements
issues.body:
## Problem

Hitlist marks papers from the PMID-override list as mono-allelic (`is_monoallelic=True`), but the per-peptide allele attribution is only as good as what IEDB ingested.  For several canonical mono-allelic studies, IEDB stored just the meta-class `\"HLA class I\"` in the `MHC Restriction` column instead of the specific 4-digit allele each peptide was measured on — even though that allele is known and published in the paper's supplementary tables.

Result: a peptide row looks like \`is_monoallelic=True, mhc_restriction=\"HLA class I\"\`, which is provenance-honest but **informationally broken**.  Users can't filter by allele, build allele-specific training sets, or align peptides to HLA-A*02:01-typed patients.

## Quantifying the gap

```
Total mono-allelic Class-I human observations: 579,096
  - four_digit allele:                         534,900 (92.4%)
  - class_only (\"HLA class I\"):                40,083 (6.9%)
  - serological (\"HLA-B27\", etc.):              4,113 (0.7%)

Mono-allelic rows WITHOUT four_digit allele:    44,196 (7.6%)
```

Worst offenders (mono-allelic + non-four-digit restriction):

| PMID       | Study                                          | Rows   | IEDB's restriction      |
|------------|------------------------------------------------|-------:|-------------------------|
| 31844290   | Sarkizova 2020 (95-allele mono-allelic)        | 36,353 | \"HLA class I\"           |
| 26154972   | —                                              |  4,096 | HLA-B27/B39/B40 (serological) |
| 27846572   | —                                              |  3,206 | \"HLA class I\"           |
| 27920218   | —                                              |    515 | \"HLA class I\"           |
| 30778243   | —                                              |      9 | \"HLA class I\"           |

Sarkizova 2020 is the extreme case: **every peptide was measured on a known single HLA allele** across a 95-allele panel, but IEDB only stored the class.  The per-peptide allele mapping exists in the paper's supplement (Table S1 / S2 lists peptide → allele).

## Proposal

1. **Add a per-PMID supplement ingestion path** for mono-allelic studies where the IEDB export lost the allele.  The curation step reads a CSV/TSV keyed by (peptide, pmid) and updates \`mhc_restriction\` at build time, pulling the 4-digit allele from the paper.

2. **Treat \`is_monoallelic=True\` without a specific allele as a curation error**, not a valid data state.  Either:
   - Promote to a specific allele via (1) (preferred), or
   - Mark the row as \`curation_allele_pending\` / exclude from mono-allelic results with a warning, so downstream tools don't mistake \"HLA class I\" for a usable restriction.

3. **Add a build-time audit** listing PMIDs where mono-allelic rows still lack a four-digit allele after supplement merge.  These are either missed supplements or genuinely irrecoverable cases — the audit makes the gap visible instead of silent.

## Why this matters

The whole point of hitlist over raw IEDB is curation — resolving exactly these kinds of gaps.  \"The provenance is honest but the data is missing\" isn't a good resting place for 44k rows (7.6% of mono-allelic Class I); most of those are recoverable from public paper supplements.

### Priority starting points (covers most of the gap)

- **PMID 31844290 — Sarkizova et al. 2020** — supplement Table S1 has per-peptide allele for all 79+16 cell lines.  One merge unlocks 36k rows (~82% of the gap).
- **PMID 27846572 / 27920218** — ~3.7k rows between them, likely same playbook.

### Data model note

If the source paper reports multiple alleles per peptide (e.g. co-elution across two mono-allelic replicates that share a peptide), the semicolon-joined list convention already used for \`gene_names\` in 1.6.0 could extend here.  But the common case is single-allele per peptide row.

## Downstream

Found while building tsarina's \`--mono-allelic-only\` flag, which currently returns rows with \`mhc_restriction=\"HLA class I\"\` — useful for provenance but not actionable for allele-specific downstream analyses.  A user asking \"show me mono-allelic PRAME peptides on A*02:01\" gets ~0 rows when the real answer probably includes many Sarkizova 2020 hits that were just unlabeled.

issues.title: engineering_drift_audit: 71 arms silent on an engineering column a sibling asserts
issues.body:
Split out of #586 / #587, where `hitlist.qc.engineering_drift_audit` was added and immediately surfaced this.

> **Kept current.** This body is rewritten whenever the audit changes, rather than corrected in a comment — a stale instruction in an issue body is the same trap #587 hit four times: guidance that no longer matches the data or no longer loads. Last verified against Hitlist 1.82.11 / #720: **55 findings across 9 studies**, 39 `error` / 16 `warn`.

## The rule

An arm that is **silent** (`""`) on an `ENGINEERING_CONDITION_COLUMNS` value a **same-material sibling asserts** is flagged. Since #576 the engineered flag is per arm, so one blanked arm is already the #586 defect: `""` means "not established", the arm stops satisfying `is_engineered_material()`, and `resolve_sample_expression_anchor` hands it the reference line's RNA at **tier 1** — reported as RNA measured in the sample — while its sibling correctly resolves at tier 2.

`none` is a curated claim of absence and passes. PMID 40113210's `hap1_wildtype` is the worked example: it sits beside eleven knockout siblings and does **not** flag, because someone curated `none` onto it.

Run it with `hitlist qc engineering-drift [--severity warn|error]`, or find it under `engineering_drift` in `hitlist qc`.

## What it flags today

| PMID | findings | err | warn | columns | study |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 31495665 | 20 | 6 | 14 | mhc_context, transfection | Abelin 2019 — MAPTAC HLA-II + class I |
| 32350084 | 19 | 19 | 0 | mhc_context | van Balen 2020 — HLA-DP allelic variants |
| 34428180 | 5 | 3 | 2 | knockout_genes, mhc_context, transduction | Son 2021 — mouse transplant tolerance |
| 38480730 | 5 | 5 | 0 | transfection | Gomez-Zepeda 2024 — Thunder-DDA-PASEF |
| 36010968 | 2 | 2 | 0 | genetic_variants, transfection | Vadakekolathu 2022 — SaOS-2 p53 |
| 29769354 | 1 | 1 | 0 | overexpression_genes | Sanz-Bravo 2018b — ERAP2 overexpression |
| 30778243 | 1 | 1 | 0 | mhc_context | Koutsakos 2019 — influenza A/B/C |
| 34006841 | 1 | 1 | 0 | mhc_context | Hensen / Habel 2021 — HLA-A*24:02 |
| 36796642 | 1 | 1 | 0 | mhc_context | Pyke / SHERPA 2023 |

The exact set is in `tests/data/engineering_drift_baseline.yaml`, keyed `<condition_id>|<column>|<severity>` and asserted by **equality** in `tests/test_qc.py` — new drift fails CI, an entry fixed in the YAML but left in the baseline fails too, and a `warn` that becomes an `error` cannot reuse its entry.

**Changelog of removals** — each recorded so the falling count is auditable rather than mysterious:

- *71 → 69:* **PMID 27862975** dropped out. Its siblings asserted only `soluble_mhc`, a capture token, so nothing was engineered on either side and no tier differed — those findings were never drift.
- *69 → 66:* **PMID 33592498**'s three parental class-I arms (`hrog02_parental_class_i`, `hrog17_parental_class_i`, `ra_parental_class_i`) dropped out because #584 curated `condition_transduction: "none"` onto them. **This is the first real fix of debt recorded here**, and it is shape A resolved exactly as intended: a genuine parental arm beside a transduced sibling, annotated with the claim of absence rather than left silent. The baseline-equality assertion caught the stale entries on merge and named all three.
- *66 → 59:* **#716** recorded seven source-backed `none` claims for control arms in PMIDs 27371725, 30573663, 31092671, 32161166 and 36215666. The audit fell from 47 `error` / 19 `warn` to 43 / 16, with no change to any arm's engineered-material verdict or expression tier. PMID 29769354 remains open under #715 because its PF-GFP control is transduced.
- *59 → 55:* **#720** recorded four source-backed `none` claims for the parental wild-type THP-1 and primary hMDM arms in PMID 39438697. The audit fell from 43 `error` / 16 `warn` to 39 / 16. The four arms retained their unengineered verdicts and expression-anchor tiers.

## The remedies, and what the loader demands of each

Every remedy below was verified by running it through `load_pmid_overrides()`; `tests/test_qc.py` keeps them honest.

| remedy | the loader demands |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | only in the six engineering columns that permit it — **never** `condition_mhc_context` |
| `mhc_genotype` + `mhc_genotype_cell` + `mhc_genotype_source` | **all three together**; `mhc_genotype_cell` alone is rejected. `mhc_genotype` is ploidy-audited and checked against `mhc_genotype_complete_loci` |
| `sample_group` | on **every** arm of the study, and **not** one group per arm — so it **cannot** separate a two-arm study at all |

That last constraint decides the approach for 30778243, 34006841 and 36796642 (2–3 arms each): `sample_group` is unavailable to them, so the `mhc_genotype` trio is the only route.

## Two shapes of work

**A. A genuine wild-type or untreated arm beside an engineered sibling** — remedy `none`. Still a positive claim about an experiment, so it needs its own Methods check; no bulk application. The THP-1 wild-type and primary hMDM arms of 39438697 were cleared in #720; PMID 36215666's mock and siCTRL controls were cleared in #716.

**B. Arms that are different materials grouped together.** `sample_group` is unset on **all 9 remaining** studies, so a study's arms collapse into one group unless `mhc_genotype` or a context column separates them. 38480730 is the clearest: HeLa, a commercial human plasma pool, JY, Raji and SK-MEL-37 in one group, where the single transfected arm makes the other five look silent.

31495665 (MAPTAC) and 32350084 (HLA-DP variants) are together **39 of the 55** and are probably mostly shape B — each arm is a different mono-allelic construct.

## Why expression tiers are NOT demoted on silence

**The baseline is not "accepted forever"** — it is debt with a known reason it cannot be paid by code alone.

The obvious fix, demoting an arm to tier 2 whenever a same-material sibling is engineered, would key expression resolution off **this audit's grouping**, which shape B shows is unreliable. Demoting 38480730's five arms would report *the wrong parent line's RNA as a surrogate* for four unrelated materials — a new and less visible error than the one it fixes.

So: **fix the grouping first, then reconsider resolution.** Until material identity is trustworthy, the honest behaviour is what ships today — those arms resolve at tier 1 and the audit says loudly which are suspect.

## Known gaps the audit deliberately does not catch

- **`condition_mhc_context` cannot state absence.** It is the one engineering column `NONE_PERMITTED_CONDITION_COLUMNS` excludes, so an arm whose MHC genuinely is not introduced has no token to say so and its finding cannot be cleared by curation at all. Fixing that means permitting `none` there — a vocabulary change worth its own discussion.
- **A capture-only `condition_mhc_context` is not treated as silence**, for the same reason. PMID 28514659's `721_221_transfectant_shla_b_46_01` and `..._b_15_01` are 721.221 **transfectants** curated `soluble_mhc` alone, so they read as unengineered and are not flagged.

## Suggested order

1. Resolve PMID 29769354's PF/PF-GFP arm identity in #715 before any absence claim.
2. 28514659's two transfectant arms, above.
3. Shape B via the `mhc_genotype` trio for the 2–3 arm studies (30778243, 34006841, 36796642).
   *(33592498 is done — #584 resolved its three via `none`.)*
4. 38480730 — the clearest multi-material group, and the best test of whether fixing grouping is enough to revisit tier resolution.
5. 31495665 and 32350084 last: 39 of the 55, and worth deciding the MAPTAC / DP-construct convention once rather than per arm.

Every fix removes its entry from `tests/data/engineering_drift_baseline.yaml` in the same PR, which the equality assertion enforces.

The YAML override system currently captures biological metadata (perturbations, HLA alleles, tissue, disease) but not mass spectrometry technical metadata. For training models and comparing across studies, we need:

### Fields to add to ms_samples entries

| Field | Examples | Why it matters |
|-------|---------|----------------|
| `ip_antibody` | W6/32, L243, MAPTAC/streptavidin, anti-b2m | Different antibodies capture different subsets |
| `acquisition_mode` | DDA, DIA, PRM, SRM/MRM | DIA gives more complete coverage; PRM/SRM are targeted |
| `instrument` | Q Exactive HF, Orbitrap Fusion, timsTOF Pro | Sensitivity/speed affects peptide yield |
| `fragmentation` | HCD, CID, ETD, EThcD | Affects peptide ID rates (EThcD ~3x more IDs) |
| `labeling` | label-free, TMT, SILAC, SIL/hipMHC | Quantitative vs qualitative; SILAC distinguishes sources |
| `search_engine` | MaxQuant, PEAKS, Proteome Discoverer, Mascot | Affects FDR and peptide assignment |
| `fdr` | 1%, 5% | Critical for data quality |

### Current state
- `pulldown_antibody` exists on ~15 entries but is inconsistent
- No acquisition mode, instrument, labeling, or search engine tracked
- Some of this can be inferred from IEDB "Assay Comments" field

### Impact on training
- DDA vs DIA datasets have different biases (DDA undersamples, DIA has deconvolution artifacts)
- TMT-labeled samples should be handled differently in quantitative models
- SILAC/hipMHC studies have internal standards useful for benchmarking
- EThcD studies find ~3x more peptides (Mommen 2014) — training on mixed fragmentation types introduces bias

### Studies with known labeling/special methods
- 32502341 (Pfammatter): TMT-labeled
- 24715725 (Bourdetsky): SILAC DRiPs
- 32488085 (Stopfer): hipMHC internal standards
- 31495665 (Abelin): MAPTAC streptavidin pulldown
- 24616531 (Mommen): EThcD fragmentation
- 28834231 (Ritz): DIA acquisition

issues.title: PyPI deploy blocked: project size quota exceeded (v1.34.0 unpublished)
issues.body:
## Problem

`./deploy.sh` (and direct `twine upload`) for **v1.34.0** fails at the PyPI upload step:

```
400 Bad Request
  400 Project size too large. Limit for project 'hitlist' total ...
```

v1.34.0 is **merged to main (#302) but NOT published to PyPI** (latest on PyPI is 1.33.2). This blocks every future release until resolved — it's a hard PyPI-side quota, not a transient error (the wheel uploads to 100% then PyPI rejects it).

## Root cause

Each release is ~90 MB (45.9 MB wheel + 45.9 MB sdist). The cumulative size across all published versions has hit PyPI's per-project total-size limit (10 GB default). The package is large because it **bundles big data files in the wheel**:

| File | Size |
|---|---|
| `hitlist/data/bulk_proteomics/bekker_jensen_2017_peptides.csv.gz` | 35.1 MB |
| `hitlist/data/supplementary/strazar_2023_hla2.csv` | 13.9 MB (**uncompressed**) |
| `hitlist/data/bulk_proteomics/bekker_jensen_2017_protein_abundance.csv.gz` | 4.4 MB |
| `hitlist/data/bulk_proteomics/ccle_nusinow_2020.csv.gz` | 1.7 MB |
| `hitlist/data/supplementary/abelin_2019_maptac_class2.csv` | 1.6 MB (uncompressed) |
| several `gomez_zepeda_2024_*.csv`, `shapiro_2025_*.csv` | uncompressed |

## Remedies

**Immediate (unblocks publishing — requires PyPI account action, cannot be done from code):**
1. **Request a project size-limit increase** for `hitlist` at https://github.com/pypi/support/issues (PyPI grants these routinely with a one-line justification), **or**
2. Delete old pre-1.30 releases on PyPI to reclaim space (destructive — breaks anyone pinned to them).

**Structural (shrinks every future release; reduces quota pressure):**
3. **Stop bundling the large bulk-proteomics / supplementary CSVs in the wheel.** They could be downloaded on first use into `~/.hitlist/` like the main corpus already is, instead of vendored into every release. Cutting the 35 MB + 14 MB files alone roughly halves the wheel.
4. **gzip the uncompressed CSVs** (`strazar_2023_hla2.csv` 14→~3 MB, `abelin_2019_maptac_class2.csv`, `gomez_zepeda_2024_*.csv`, `shapiro_2025_*.csv`) — a quick win even if they stay bundled.

## Status
- Code for v1.34.0 (`pmhc --species` / `--source-context`) is on `main`; only the PyPI publish is blocked.
- Recommend #1 (size-limit increase) to unblock now, then #3/#4 as a follow-up to stop the bloat recurring.

issues.title: APM per-gene flags are contaminated by study-level perturbations: control arms flagged as knockouts
issues.body:
## Problem

`apm_columns_for_sample()` derives the per-gene APM flags from the sample's own `condition` **unioned with the parent study's `perturbations` list**:

```python
# hitlist/export.py:432
row.update(
    apm_columns_for_sample(
        condition,
        perturbations=study_perturbations,   # <-- study-level, not sample-level
    )
)
```

For any study that curates a *panel* of perturbations, the study-level list names every gene in the panel, so **every arm of that study — including the untreated control — is flagged as perturbed for every gene.**

## Reproduction

Shapiro 2025 HAP1 APM CRISPR KO panel (PMID 40113210), 12 arms:

```python
from hitlist.export import generate_ms_samples_table
s = generate_ms_samples_table()
sub = s[s['pmid'].astype(str) == '40113210']
print(sub[['sample_label','condition_category','apm_perturbed',
           'apm_erap1_perturbed','apm_genes_perturbed']].to_string(index=False))
```

```
 sample_label  condition_category          apm_perturbed  apm_erap1_perturbed  apm_genes_perturbed
HAP1 wildtype  unperturbed                          True                 True  b2m;tap1;tap2;tapbp;erap1;pdia3;calr;canx;irf2;ganab;sppl3
  HAP1 B2M KO  MHC-I_loss_B2M                       True                 True  b2m;tap1;tap2;tapbp;erap1;pdia3;calr;canx;irf2;ganab;sppl3
 HAP1 TAP1 KO  TAP_perturbation                     True                 True  b2m;tap1;tap2;tapbp;erap1;pdia3;calr;canx;irf2;ganab;sppl3
HAP1 ERAP1 KO  ERAP1_perturbation                   True                 True  b2m;tap1;tap2;tapbp;erap1;pdia3;calr;canx;irf2;ganab;sppl3
... all 12 arms identical ...
```

The wildtype control claims `apm_erap1_perturbed=True`. Every arm claims all 11 genes.

## Blast radius (current corpus, v1.45.0)

- **184 of 688 `ms_samples` rows, spanning 22 PMIDs**, are flagged `apm_perturbed=True` while their own `condition_category` is `unperturbed`.
- 12 samples claim all 11 genes at once; 17 claim 2.

Affected control arms include `721.221-B*51:01 wildtype` (flagged `erap1;erap2`), `C1R HLA-B*40:02 (WT)` (flagged `erap2`), `A375 melanoma (untreated)` (flagged `erap1`), `A549 lung cancer (untreated)` (flagged `ifn_gamma;tnf_alpha`), `mouse splenocytes (WT)` (flagged `hla_do`), and all 11 `MAPTAC-HLA-*` samples (flagged `hla_dm`).

## Consequences

1. `--apm-only` / `apm_only=True` sweeps control arms into the "perturbed" set. On observations that is 1.1M rows where the KO-vs-WT contrast is the whole point.
2. Per-gene filtering (`apm_erap1_perturbed`) is unusable — it selects entire studies, not ERAP1-perturbed samples.
3. `apm_genes_perturbed` is a study-level fact wearing a sample-level column name, so it silently reads as "this sample had these genes perturbed".

This is the same class as #344 — a silently wrong result, not a crash.

## The signal that *is* correct

`perturbation` and `condition_category` derive from the sample's own condition only, and they are right: the HAP1 wildtype arm correctly reads `condition_category == "unperturbed"` with an empty `perturbation`.

## Proposed fix

- Derive `apm_<gene>_perturbed` / `apm_perturbed` / `apm_genes_perturbed` from the **sample's own condition only**.
- Move the study-level union into separate, explicitly-named columns (e.g. `study_apm_genes` / `study_apm_perturbed`) so the panel context is still queryable without being mistaken for a per-sample fact.
- Keep `apm_only` filtering on the sample-level union flag.

## Acceptance criteria

- `HAP1 wildtype` reports `apm_perturbed=False`, `apm_genes_perturbed=""`.
- `HAP1 ERAP1 KO` reports `apm_genes_perturbed="erap1"`, not all 11 genes.
- No sample has `apm_perturbed=True` while `condition_category == "unperturbed"`.
- Study-panel context remains reachable through the new study-level columns.

issues.title: Curate source_tissue / cell type for PMIDs with blank provenance (PRAME '(unspecified)' rows)
issues.body:
## Problem

Some immunopeptidome PMIDs leave IEDB's `source_tissue` blank, so their peptides land in an uninformative `(unspecified)` bucket in `hitlist pmhc --gene <X> --by-tissue`. Surfaced via PRAME — 9 observations / 8 peptides with no tissue. These are real evidence (epitope-discovery / ligandome / transfectant papers) that should carry a curated `source_tissue` and/or `cell_name`/`cell_type` so they reason correctly through the cancer-vs-healthy and tissue-vs-cell-line splits.

## The PRAME-surfaced PMIDs (verify each against the paper, then curate)

| PMID | Study | Likely correct provenance (verify) |
|---|---|---|
| 28628042 | TCR-mimic therapeutic antibody targeting tumor-associated PRAME | tumor cell line(s) — assign `cell_name`/tissue from Methods |
| 29712860 | HLA-I C-terminal-extension ligandome (methods) | source cell line(s) used for the ligandome (likely a B-LCL / standard line) |
| 31495665 | Abelin 2019 **MAPTAC** (3 peptides; HEK293/A375/Expi293 transfectant system; `disease=healthy`) | already `cell_name="MAPTAC"`; set `source_tissue`/cell_type to the transfectant lines so it's not "(unspecified)" |
| 31575892 | Multiple myeloma HLA-I T-cell epitopes | myeloma — Blood / Bone Marrow (patient cells or myeloma line) |
| 40008881 | HCC (hepatocellular carcinoma) HLA-A\*02:01 epitopes | Liver / HCC cell line |

(8 peptides total here — but this is a **pattern**, not just PRAME: any gene query hits the same `(unspecified)` bucket for these and similar blank-tissue PMIDs.)

## Scope / approach
1. For each PMID above, read the Methods and add `source_tissue` (and `cell_name`/cell type where it's a line) via the supplementary manifest defaults (for supplementary entries like 31495665) or a per-PMID curation path.
2. Broader: enumerate **all** medium-confidence PMIDs with blank `source_tissue` but a known cell line / disease, and curate them (a `qc` audit could list `source_tissue == "" AND src_cancer/cell_line set` grouped by PMID).
3. This mirrors the per-paper species curation done in v1.34.2 (#305) — explicit, no silent defaults.

## Why it matters
`--by-tissue` (v1.34.3–v1.34.8) is now a real antigen-reasoning tool (healthy-tissue safety signal, cancer tissue vs cancer cell-line). Blank-tissue rows weaken it — they're evidence that can't be placed. Curating provenance makes every observation interpretable.

Related: #305 (per-paper curation), the `--by-tissue` / `--source-context` work.

issues.title: Scanner: split cell_name into cell_line_name + cell_type at build time
issues.body:
## Problem

`hitlist/scanner.py:73` reads IEDB's `Cell Name` field into the `cell_name` column verbatim.  Across 4.4M rows the field carries three different shapes:

1. **Pure cell-line names** (~400K rows): `Expi293F`, `MAPTAC`, `Raji`, `JY`, `HAP1 wildtype`, `HAP1 CALR KO`
2. **Pure cell-type names** (~3M rows): `B cell` (693K), `Splenocyte`, `Other`, `PBMC`, `Lymphoblast`, `Thymocyte`, `Lymphocyte`, `Dendritic cell`, `Melanocyte`, `Fibroblast`, `Hepatocyte`, `Glial cell`, `Lymph node cells`, `Epithelial cell`, `Cell found in tissue` (1.1M)
3. **Hybrid `<line>-<type>`** (~700K rows in top 40 alone): `C1R cells-B cell` (255K), `K562-Myeloid cell` (46K), `HeLa cells-Epithelial cell` (62K), `MDA-MB-231-Epithelial cell` (96K), `LM-MEL-44-Melanocyte` (66K), `JY cells-B cell` (28K), `A549-Epithelial cell` (24K), `HROG17-Glial Cell` (21K), `293-T-Epithelial cell` (19K), `MAVER-1-Lymphoblast` (15K), `MCF-7/LY2-Epithelial cell` (13K), ...

So one column conflates three semantically distinct things.  `src_cell_line` partly disambiguates (True for shapes 1 + 3, False for shape 2) but the hybrid case still carries both pieces of info in one string.

## Proposed split

At scanner build time, parse `cell_name` into two derived columns:

- `cell_line_name` (already exists) — the line part, when present.  Already populated for shapes 1 + 3 via `classify_ms_row`.
- `cell_type` (NEW) — the type part, when present.

For each row:

| `src_cell_line` | `cell_name` shape | `cell_line_name` | `cell_type` |
|---|---|---|---|
| True | pure line (`Expi293F`) | `Expi293F` | `""` (unknown) |
| True | hybrid (`K562-Myeloid cell`) | `K562` | `Myeloid cell` |
| False | pure type (`B cell`) | `""` | `B cell` |
| False | none (`Other`, `Cell found in tissue`) | `""` | `""` (unknown / not recorded) |

## Implementation

Parsing the hybrid case requires a known cell-type vocabulary, not just a regex.  Edge cases:
- `HCT 116-Epithelial cell` — space in the line name
- `LM-MEL-44-Melanocyte` — three hyphens, only the last separates type
- `293-T-Epithelial cell` — line contains hyphen
- `MCF-7/LY2-Epithelial cell` — slash + hyphen mix

Algorithm: split on the last `-`; if the right side matches a known cell-type label (`Epithelial cell`, `B cell`, `Myeloid cell`, `Melanocyte`, `Hepatocyte`, `Glial cell`, `Lymphoblast`, `Monocyte`, `Endothelial cell`, ...), treat as hybrid; else treat the whole string as a line.  The vocabulary should be a small curated YAML list (~20 entries cover >95% of the corpus).

## Downstream wins

- `hitlist pmhc --cell-type "Melanocyte"` filter (probably as a separate #259-style enhancement once `cell_type` is on the parquet)
- Cleaner exports for downstream consumers (tsarina, training-table generation)
- More accurate cell_type — line counts in n_samples decomposition (#260 currently uses `cell_line_name` which is correct for the line dimension, but downstream queries that group by cell_type today have to parse cell_name themselves)

## Out of scope

- Renaming `cell_name` itself.  Keep it as the raw upstream string for traceability.
- Cellosaurus / Ontology integration for the cell-type vocabulary.  Start with a flat YAML list of the common categories, upgrade later if needed.
- Backfilling `cell_type` for the rare `Other` / `Cell found in tissue` rows — those represent genuine curation gaps upstream, not parsing failures.

## Reference

Surfaced in the #260 review of `pmhc_query` n_samples decomposition.  #260 ships a working `n_cell_lines` / `n_donors` / `n_donor_cell_types` decomposition that doesn't NEED this split (it uses `cell_line_name` directly), but downstream filtering by cell_type does.

issues.title: Class-II 'implausible' threshold at ≥31aa flags ~13K legitimate Stražar 2023 peptides
issues.body:
## Background

v1.30.17 (#201) introduced four severity tiers for `mhc_class_label_severity`. The class-II `implausible` cutoff is currently:

> class II ≤4 or **≥31** aa → implausible

After the v1.30.20 PTM-suffix fix, the production parquet has **16,885 class-II rows tagged implausible**. The breakdown:

| PMID | Source | Rows | Study |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 37301199 | supplement | **13,268** | Stražar 2023 — HLA-II mono-allelic |
| 31495665 | supplement | 1,600 | Abelin 2019 — MAPTAC (class II portion) |
| 33968037 | iedb | 858 | TNBC IFNγ class II |
| 33043033 | iedb | 414 | IFN-induced class II changes on DR molecules |
| (other) | iedb | ~745 | various |

**78% are Stražar 2023 alone**, all from the curated paper supplement (`hitlist/data/supplementary/strazar_2023_hla2.csv`). Length distribution there:

```
count    308,418
mean      19.3 aa
max       51 aa
13,268 rows >= 31 aa
```

These aren't curation drift — the Stražar paper specifically reports mono-allelic class-II ligands up to 51aa.

## Why this matters

Users who pass `--exclude-class-label-implausible` (or `load_observations(exclude_class_label_implausible=True)`, both shipped in v1.30.18) currently lose ~13K legitimate Stražar mono-allelic class-II peptides. That's exactly the high-quality training data the filter is meant to preserve.

## Options

**A. Raise the implausible threshold** to `≥35` or `≥40`:
- Most class-II ligand papers report up to 30aa; HLA-DM-edited / unconventional class-II peptides extend to ~40-50aa per the literature.
- A threshold of `≥40` would keep ~16,400 of the 16,885 currently-implausible rows in `ok`/`borderline`, dropping only ~485 rows that are >=40aa — which are still rare enough to be worth flagging.
- Symmetric concern: raising the threshold lets through actually-mislabeled rows (class-I peptides with class-II label that happen to be 31-39aa) — but those would already be implausible-as-class-I rows (≥18aa class I), so they're caught regardless.

**B. Add a `borderline-long` tier** to mark 31-50aa as worth flagging but not implausible. Doubles the column complexity for marginal benefit.

**C. Per-source-organism / per-PMID override.** Heavy machinery; skip.

**D. Status quo** — accept that the implausible filter drops ~13K Stražar rows and document it.

## Recommendation

**Option A with threshold `≥40`** is the cleanest. The literature is reasonably consistent on \"normal\" class-II being ≤30aa, but reports of DM-edited / extended class-II ligands routinely span into the 30-40aa range. `≥40` lines up with the empirical break in Stražar's distribution (rows 30-39aa are fairly dense; 40+ aa are rare).

Symmetrically, the class-I implausible threshold of `≥18` should stay — bulged class-I peptides are well-documented but cap around 17aa.

Want me to ship A as v1.30.22? It's a one-line change in `hitlist/observations.py` plus adjusting the regression test.

## Related

- #201 (introduced the four-tier severity)
- #206 / v1.30.20 (the PTM-suffix fix that surfaced this signal cleanly)
issues.display_title: Class-II 'implausible' threshold at ≥31aa flags ~13K legitimate Stražar 2023 peptides

issues.title: Match Abelin MAPTAC class-II DP/DQ supplementary rows to curated heterodimer samples
issues.body:
## Audit finding

Abelin 2019 MAPTAC class-II supplementary rows and `ms_samples` use incompatible class-II allele representations for DP/DQ.

Current curation:
- `pmid_overrides.yaml` stores MAPTAC DP/DQ samples as heterodimer-like strings such as `HLA-DPB1*06:01/DPA1*01:03` and `HLA-DQB1*06:04/DQA1*01:02`.
- `abelin_2019_maptac_class2.csv` stores the corresponding peptide restrictions as beta-chain-only `HLA-DPB1*06:01` and `HLA-DQB1*06:04`.

Local audit evidence:
- 4,587 rows have `HLA-DPB1*06:01`.
- 1,964 rows have `HLA-DQB1*06:04`.
- Total affected class-II MAPTAC rows: 6,551.

## Impact

These rows cannot exact-match the curated sample metadata and fall back to class/paper-level metadata instead of carrying the correct mono-allelic MAPTAC sample context. This weakens allele-level class-II training exports and sample provenance.

## Suggested fix

- Normalize class-II pair/component matching so a beta-chain-only restriction can match a curated DP/DQ heterodimer sample when unambiguous.
- Alternatively, add explicit beta-chain aliases to the `ms_samples` metadata and teach the join to use them.
- Add a regression for `HLA-DPB1*06:01` and `HLA-DQB1*06:04` rows from PMID `31495665` proving they join to the MAPTAC sample rather than the class pool.

issues.title: Per-sample custom reference proteomes (host + viruses + transfectants)
issues.body:
## Problem
Currently flanking mapping uses `source_organism` per observation to select a reference proteome from the curated registry. This misses several important cases:

1. **EBV-LCL cell lines** (JY, Raji, B-LCLs): peptides may derive from EBV proteins, but we only map against human. We have `ebv: UP000153037` in VIRAL_PROTEOMES but it's not wired into the flanking step per-sample.

2. **Viral infection studies**: PMIDs like 35051231 (influenza A), 32157095 (SARS-CoV-2) search against host + specific viruses. A peptide like `GILGFVFTL` (influenza M1) should map to the viral proteome for that sample, not the human Ensembl.

3. **Transfected/engineered cell lines**: SARS-CoV-2-spike-transfected JY, HLA-transfected 721.221, etc. — these have additional proteins the paper searched against.

4. **Multi-proteome searches**: some studies search host + 2-3 viruses at once.

## Proposed data model

Extend `ms_samples` in `pmid_overrides.yaml`:

```yaml
ms_samples:
  - type: "JY + SARS-CoV-2 spike"
    mhc_class: "I"
    mhc: "HLA-A*02:01 HLA-B*07:02 HLA-C*07:02"
    reference_proteomes:
      - uniprot: UP000005640          # human Ensembl / UniProt
      - uniprot: UP000153037          # EBV (B-LCL)
      - uniprot: UP000464024          # SARS-CoV-2
      - key: sars-cov-2-spike-s1      # optional alias to VIRAL_PROTEOMES
```

Flanking step: for each observation in this sample, try all listed proteomes in order and take the first match. Add `flanking_proteome_source` column to distinguish (`"host"` / `"ebv"` / `"sars-cov-2"`).

## Scope
- Extend `ms_samples` schema validation
- Wire `_add_flanking` to consult per-sample list (falls back to `source_organism` lookup)
- Auto-download any referenced UPIDs
- Add `flanking_proteome_source` column to output

## Priority candidates
- All EBV-LCL PMIDs (Gomez-Zepeda, Bassani-Sternberg, Chong 2018) — trivial to add EBV
- PMID 35051231 (Nicholas 2022 influenza)
- PMID 31495665 (Abelin 2019 — MAPTAC in expi293, would need HEK293 proteome override)

issues.title: Curate bulk (non-MHC) proteomics in a separate index for detectability priors
issues.body:
## Motivation

Right now hitlist indexes MHC-restricted MS evidence (ligandomes, elution assays) — and, separately, binding assays once #47 lands. A third category that belongs in the library is **bulk proteomics** on the same cell lines and tissues: whole-cell tryptic digests, deep proteome drafts, CPTAC tumor proteomes, etc.

The reason to curate this upstream rather than have each downstream tool re-scrape PRIDE/MassIVE/CPTAC: estimating **MS detectability bias by sequence content**. When a peptide is missing from an MHC-I ligandome, we'd like to know whether the parent protein is even expressed/detectable in that sample in general — otherwise "not presented" and "not detectable" collapse into the same observation.

## Proposal

Build a sibling `bulk_proteomics.parquet` alongside `observations.parquet` (MS, existing) and `binding_assays.parquet` (#47), keyed on **sample** (cell line, tissue, donor) rather than MHC allele.

### Schema sketch

| Column | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| `peptide` | tryptic (mostly) — caveat below |
| `protein_id`, `gene_name`, `gene_id` | from proteome sidecar, semicolon-joined for ambiguous mappings |
| `sample_id` | canonical cell line name (Cellosaurus CVCL_), tissue, or donor ID |
| `sample_kind` | `cell_line` / `tissue_tumor` / `tissue_normal` / `body_fluid` |
| `cell_line_name` | free-text (for cross-reference with `observations.cell_line_name`) |
| `tissue` | OBO-style tissue term when applicable |
| `disease` | free-text diagnosis where applicable |
| `protease` | `trypsin` / `lysc` / `aspn` / `chymotrypsin` / `multi` / `unknown` |
| `instrument` | Orbitrap Fusion, Q-Exactive, timsTOF, etc. |
| `intensity` | normalized abundance (log2 iBAQ or log2 LFQ) when available |
| `ms_level` | DDA vs DIA |
| `pmid`, `pxd_id` | PRIDE/MassIVE accession + paper |
| `source` | `ccle` / `cptac` / `kim2014` / `wilhelm2014` / `proteomicsdb` / `nci60` / ... |
| `is_contaminant` | cRAP/Krogan flagged |

### Candidate sources (first pass)

- **CCLE proteomics** — Nusinow et al. 2020 (Cell). ~375 cell lines, 11-plex TMT, tryptic. Direct overlap with many ligandome papers.
- **NCI-60** — Gholami et al. 2013. Tryptic, 60 lines.
- **Kim et al. 2014** and **Wilhelm et al. 2014** — draft human proteomes. Tissue-level, tryptic. Known to have contamination issues (Ezkurdia review); flag conservatively.
- **ProteomicsDB** — aggregated reference.
- **CPTAC** — tumor-matched bulk proteomes across BRCA, COAD, GBM, HNSCC, LUAD, OV, UCEC. Tissue-level, TMT, tryptic.
- **Geiger et al. 2012** — 11-cell-line super-SILAC tryptic reference.

### API sketch

\`\`\`python
from hitlist.bulk import load_bulk_proteomics

# Does the parent protein show up in any bulk MS run on this cell line?
load_bulk_proteomics(cell_line=\"A375\", gene_name=\"PRAME\")

# Peptide-level detectability lookup — is this exact tryptic peptide ever seen?
load_bulk_proteomics(peptide=\"LYVDSLFFL\")

# Aggregate to protein-level detection matrix
load_bulk_proteomics(sample_kind=\"cell_line\").groupby([\"gene_name\", \"sample_id\"])[\"intensity\"].max()
\`\`\`

## The tryptic caveat (important)

Bulk proteomics is overwhelmingly **tryptic** (cleaves C-term of K/R), while MHC-I ligandomes are **unrestricted** (proteasomal + aminopeptidase processing). This means:

- At the **peptide** level, you cannot directly compare \"this 9-mer was seen in MHC-I IP\" vs \"this 9-mer was seen in tryptic bulk\" — the tryptic peptide-space barely overlaps with the MHC-I peptide-space. The overlap that exists is mostly accidental (MHC-I peptide that happens to have K/R at position P1−1 and Pω).
- At the **protein** level, aggregation is clean: \"was any tryptic peptide from PRAME detected in A375 bulk MS?\" is a well-posed question and a useful prior for interpreting PRAME ligandome gaps.
- For **sequence-level detectability priors**, the right move is usually an in-silico model (DeepMSPeptide, Prosit detectability) trained on the aggregated bulk data — not direct peptide-level lookup.

**Recommendation:** ship the index with peptide-level rows (for people who want them and understand the caveat), but make the documented/blessed API protein-level aggregation. Add a `protease` column so users can subset to the (rare) non-tryptic bulk datasets if they want apples-to-apples peptide comparisons.

## Why separate file (not a kind-flag on observations)

Same reasoning as #47, plus:

1. **Different keys.** `observations.parquet` is peptide × allele. `bulk_proteomics.parquet` is peptide × sample. Joining them on either key drops most rows.
2. **Different scale.** CCLE + CPTAC + drafts is on the order of 10⁷–10⁸ peptide-sample rows. Mixing into observations would dominate the file.
3. **Different trust model.** Bulk MS detection is much noisier than targeted ligandome IP; conflating them in one table confuses per-row quality heuristics.

## Downstream impact

- **tsarina** — `tsarina hits --gene PRAME --allele HLA-A*24:02` could report \"PRAME protein is detected in bulk MS on cell line X at rank Y\" as a sanity check beside ligandome hits. Eventually: a `--require-bulk-detection` flag that only shows MHC-I hits whose parent protein is actually expressed in the sample's lineage.
- **Ligandome QC** — lets you flag studies where the MHC-I pulldown captures peptides from proteins that don't show up in bulk (contamination suspect) or conversely misses peptides from very abundant proteins (pulldown inefficiency).
- **Training data for detectability/retention models** — prebuilt index with normalized intensity is much friendlier than re-scraping PRIDE per project.

## Build/CLI surface

\`\`\`
hitlist data build                    # MS + binding (per #47)
hitlist data build --bulk             # add bulk proteomics (opt-in initially; big)
hitlist data build --bulk-sources ccle,cptac
\`\`\`

Default off until sources stabilize and size is measured, since this is a multi-GB index.

## Related

- hitlist#47 — binding-assay index (same separation-of-concerns pattern).
- hitlist#43 (closed, 1.6.0) — gene/protein annotation sidecar. The same sidecar applies here: peptide → gene_names/gene_ids/protein_ids is independent of whether the peptide came from MHC IP, in-vitro binding, or tryptic bulk.

issue.title: 469k peptide rows remain arm-ambiguous (126k in APM studies) — per-study discriminator curation
issue.body:
## Problem

After #354, rows whose experimental arm cannot be determined are marked `sample_attribution="pmid_ambiguous"` and their arm-specific fields are blanked rather than guessed. That is the correct default, but it leaves **469,327 peptide rows across 27 studies** with no usable APM / perturbation featurization — **125,945 of them in studies that ran an APM perturbation**, which is exactly the population the KO-vs-WT contrast needs.

This issue tracks working that number down by curating per-study discriminators.

## Breakdown (v1.47.0 corpus)

| PMID | ambiguous rows | curated arms | APM study |
|---|---|---|---|
| 33858848 | 255,179 | 42 | |
| 31844290 | 50,972 | 107 | yes |
| 33912179 | 32,848 | 2 | |
| 31495665 | 27,259 | 14 | yes |
| 38480730 | 24,030 | 6 | |
| 33592498 | 17,510 | 9 | yes |
| 32161166 | 11,509 | 2 | yes |
| 36010968 | 10,323 | 3 | |
| 31530632 | 10,319 | 2 | yes |
| 23481700 | 7,301 | 2 | |
| 29769354 | 4,999 | 2 | yes |
| 30524438 | 4,462 | 2 | |

`33858848` alone is over half the total and should be looked at first.

## What "curating a discriminator" means

Ranked by how much they buy:

1. **A per-row curated label.** `attributed_sample_label` already resolves PMID 31844290's patient cohort exactly (#360). Where a study's supplementary tables identify the sample per peptide, curating that into the observation rows is the strongest fix.
2. **Per-arm `cell_name` in supplementary CSVs.** How the Shapiro HAP1 panel (PMID 40113210) splits cleanly across 12 arms.
3. **Symmetric arm labels**, so a matcher can at least attribute the sample *system* — see #359.

## Known dead ends

Do not try to recover these from IEDB's narrative fields. `antigen_processing_comments` / `assay_comments` describe the study, so they name every arm on every row; scoring them is what produced the original collapse. PMID 31530632's 10,319 rows all open with "peptidomes from wild-type and ERAP2-KO cells were compared" and carry no per-row treatment signal at all. Absence of a treatment word in a comment that never discusses treatment is not evidence.

The exception, already implemented, is IEDB's structured per-peptide enumeration ("eluted from the following experimental condition(s): ..."), which is parsed and covers 168k rows across 4 PMIDs.

## Acceptance criteria

Per study, either:
- rows attribute to a specific arm, or
- the study is confirmed genuinely unresolvable from the deposited data and recorded as such, so it stops being re-investigated.
